metadata.source: U.S. Census Bureau ACS 5-Year Data Profiles & Passaic County 2026 Certified Rolls

zipCodeComparison.neighborhoodsIncluded: Belmont Ave Core & Roe St Heights, Botto House & Church St Historic District
keyFindings: Certified composite property tax rate is 5.428%, with an equalization ratio of 51.19%.
Public education represents 51.2% of property taxes, while municipal operations account for 32.4%.
Average residential assessment is $209,879, producing an average annual tax bill of $11,392.23.

neighborhoods.name: Belmont Ave Core & Roe St Heights
neighborhoods.character: Historic silk strike landmark borough (Botto House National Historic Landmark) with traditional two-family homes and single-family colonials
neighborhoods.description: Historic industrial heritage borough surrounding Botto House, home of the American Labor Museum.
neighborhoods.taxDynamic: High property tax rate (4.85%) requiring substantial state formula aid for local school district.

neighborhoods.name: Botto House & Church St Historic District
neighborhoods.character: Historic labor landmark district with single-family colonials, duplexes, and proximity to Manchester Regional High School
neighborhoods.description: Historic residential streets surrounding the Botto House National Historic Landmark.
neighborhoods.taxDynamic: Moderate assessment values with state education aid supporting local schools.

equityAnalysis.summary: Haledon Borough maintains a certified residential tax roll across its neighborhoods.

keyTakeaways.title: Property Tax Burden & Household Income
keyTakeaways.detail: In Haledon Borough, homeowners pay an average of $11,392.23 annually in property taxes, consuming approximately 13.83% of median household income.

keyTakeaways.title: Equalization Ratio & Revaluation Balance
keyTakeaways.detail: With an equalization ratio of 51.19%, assessed values average ~51.19% of current true market values, establishing the basis for certified county tax equalization.

keyTakeaways.title: School District vs Municipal Levy Split
keyTakeaways.detail: Local education represents 51.2% of the total tax bill, municipal government absorbs 32.4%, and Passaic County claims 16.4%.
